accuracy.evidence: Every figure checks: £4.50 × 30 = £135 and × 365 = £1,642.50; Jade's balanced plan is £550 + £200 + £80 + £20 + £200 + £150 = £1,200; the save-what's-left months (£1,180, £1,200, £1,260, £1,150, £1,210, £1,190 spent) leave £20 + £0 + £0 + £50 + £0 + £10 = £80, against £600 paid first; £50 a month for 24 months at 4% AER (monthly rate 1.04^(1/12) − 1, payment at month end) grows to £1,246.28, so £46.28 interest, not £96. The three-months-of-essentials emergency fund follows MoneyHelper's guidance, and the adult text tells parents to use take-home pay after tax and National Insurance. Challenge sums check: £900 − £820 = £80, £3 × 190 = £570, 5% of £100 = £5.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets: every cost is a need (step 1 sort, challenge tag 'want', p1, m5); small costs do not matter (step 3 predict £160 vs £1,600, tag 'small', p2, m2); saving what is left works (step 4 predict 'About £600' vs 'Much less', tag 'left', p4, m3); borrowing is a safety net (tag 'credit', m7); interest is the rate times everything paid in (step 5 predict '£96 (4% of £1,200, twice)', m6) and interest is the whole balance (tag 'rate': 5% of £100 is £5, not £105).

lab_distinct.evidence: No other flagship deals with money: a needs/wants drag sort, a five-row budget with a fixed rent line and a live 'every pound has a job' check, a 30-day calendar that fills with £4.50 drinks, two six-month savings lanes run side by side, and a 24-month savings chart with paid-in and interest split and a 0%/4% switch. gate_lab_distinct passes against all existing labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea comes from the learner's own actions: the budget only shows 'Every pound has a job ✓' when spending plus saving is exactly £1,200 with at least £120 saved; the calendar total climbs day by day to £135 before the yearly £1,642.50 appears; the two lanes show £80 against £600 from the same income; the green interest slice on the chart stays thin early and grows later, and switching to 0% removes it.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions with a tempting wrong answer, each disproved by the lab: '£4.50 a day, every day. Over a year that costs about…' (£160 vs £1,600), 'Jade plans to save whatever is left… In six months she saves…' (About £600 vs Much less) and '£50 a month for 2 years at 4%. The interest is about…' (£96 vs About £46). Each locks before the action and the done line names the prediction and the outcome.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six questions, each with two tagged wrong options and a reply per tag: 'want' (A want is nice to have. A need keeps you housed, fed, safe or able to work), 'calc' (add the costs and take them from the income, or multiply the daily cost by the days), 'left' (Money left in your account tends to get spent. Plan saving first), 'small' (Small costs repeat), 'credit' (Borrowing costs interest and puts you behind next month) and 'rate' (5% of £100 is £5; your total becomes £105). Option order rotates between rounds.

readability.evidence: Learner text reads at FK grade 2.8 against the 6.5 target, in lines such as 'Pay yourself first. Money left in your account tends to get spent, so move your saving on payday.' Adult text reads at 7.7 (target 9.5). Lab labels are short ('Every pound has a job ✓', 'Saved: £600', 'Paid in £1,200 · interest £46.28') and all money uses £ with UK terms (take-home pay, standing order, AER).

no_filler.evidence: gate_content finds no filler. Each learner paragraph carries one habit (needs first, small costs add up, pay yourself first, emergency fund and interest). Adult paragraphs cover take-home pay, why automatic saving works, three named mistakes with the £46 vs £96 example, and what each lab step does. Items use different contexts (drinks, snacks, rent, phone repair, boiler) and five are parameterised.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px Android (dark) and iPhone 13 (light) after Show me on all six steps. After the first pass, long card names that ran past the Needs/Wants boxes were shortened, the budget bars were moved to one shared £0–£400 scale so the £20 phone bar no longer looked as big as £200 food, and the savings lane bars were shortened so £100 labels no longer touched the lane title. Calendar days fit six to a row with 44 px targets.

accessibility.evidence: Every drag or tap has a named button: 'Rent is a need', 'Food: £10 more', 'Buy today’s drink', 'Choose: pay yourself first', 'Run next month', '+6 months', 'Switch to 0%'. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action with the whole state in words (for example 'Budget: rent £550, food £200, transport £80, phone £20, fun £200, savings £150. Total £1,200 of £1,200.'). The walkthrough's axe WCAG 2.1 AA check is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
